draft.title: Religion and festivals
card: Religion was part of daily life in Sparta. The state held many festivals in honour of the gods, and Spartans took part as a duty to them.
a festival in honour of Apollo Karneios, held in the month of Karneios in late summer. Sparta kept it as a sacred time.
a festival held at Amyklai near Sparta, linked to Apollo and the youth Hyakinthos. It was a major event in the Spartan year.

Spartans sometimes delayed going to war so they could finish a festival. Ancient writers such as Herodotus describe this, for example before the Battle of Marathon in 490 BC and when Thermopylae was defended in 480 BC.
draft.remember: Spartans took festivals so seriously that they could put off a military campaign to complete them.

a.q: What does Sparta's delay of military action for a festival show about Spartan society?
opts: Religious duties could take priority over military plans
Spartans were reluctant to fight in any war
Festivals were held only to train the army
The kings had no power over military decisions
a.why: Spartans put off campaigns to complete festivals, so religious duty could outweigh military plans. It does not show they avoided war, because the delays were sometimes only temporary and Spartans were known as strong fighters.
a.clue: Think about what was put off, and what was done first.

b.q: Herodotus says the Spartans did not send their full army to Thermopylae in 480 BC because they were holding a festival. Which view of this is best supported by the card?
opts: Religious observance could affect Spartan military timing
The festival proved Sparta had no interest in the war
Spartans never fought during any festival period
The Karneia and Hyakinthia were the same festival
b.why: The card says Spartans sometimes delayed war to complete festivals, so religion could affect timing. The festival did not mean Sparta ignored the war, because Spartans still sent a force and the delay was only sometimes applied.
b.clue: The card says sometimes, not always.

a.best: Religious duties could take priority over military plans

b.best: Religious observance could affect Spartan military timing

problems.detail: For Marathon (490 BC), Herodotus (6.106) says the Spartans could not march until the full moon because of a religious law. He does not say they were finishing a festival. Linking this delay to the Karneia is a later interpretation, so citing Herodotus for a festival delay before Marathon overstates the source. Thermopylae (Karneia and Olympic festival, Hdt 7.206) is accurate.
The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('could'). Every distractor uses an absolute ('any', 'no', 'only'), so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('could'). The distractors use absolutes ('proved', 'never'), and the clue 'sometimes, not always' points straight at the hedged option, so the answer is given away.
The why says 'the delays were sometimes only temporary', which is confusing. Delays are temporary by nature, and the card does not suggest some delays were permanent.

check.summary: Both questions have the right answer, but in each one it is the only hedged option among absolutes (and b's clue points to it), so students can guess without knowing the idea. The card also cites Herodotus for a festival delay before Marathon, when he describes a full-moon religious restriction, not a festival.

proposal.title: Religion and festivals
card: Religion was part of daily life in Sparta. The state held many festivals in honour of the gods, and Spartans took part as a duty to them.
a festival in honour of Apollo Karneios, held in the month of Karneios in late summer. Sparta kept it as a sacred time.
a festival held at Amyklai near Sparta, linked to Apollo and the youth Hyakinthos. Herodotus says it slowed Sparta's reply to an Athenian call for help in 479 BC.

Spartans sometimes delayed going to war so they could finish a festival. Herodotus says that in 480 BC Sparta sent King Leonidas ahead to Thermopylae with a small force, and the main army was to follow once the Karneia was over.
proposal.remember: Spartans could put off a campaign until a festival was complete, because religious duty mattered so much to them.

a.q: What does Sparta delaying a campaign to finish a festival show about Spartan society?
opts: Religious duty could be placed ahead of war
Spartans were unwilling to fight foreign enemies
Festivals mainly served to train the army
The kings had little say in going to war
a.why: Spartans put off campaigns until a festival was complete, so religious duty could come before military plans. It does not show they were unwilling to fight: the army still went to war once the festival was over.
a.clue: Think about what was put off, and what was done first.

b.q: In 480 BC Sparta sent Leonidas to Thermopylae with a small force instead of the full army. What reason does Herodotus give?
opts: The Karneia had to be finished before the army marched
The Hyakinthia at Amyklai had to be finished first
Sparta did not see the Persian army as a threat
Spartan law banned fighting outside the Peloponnese
b.why: Herodotus says the main army was to follow once the Karneia was over, so the festival delayed the full march. The Hyakinthia is tempting because it also delayed Sparta, but Herodotus links it to the call for help from Athens in 479 BC, not to Thermopylae.
b.clue: Which festival fell in late summer, when Persia invaded?

a.best: Religious duty could be placed ahead of war

b.best: The Karneia had to be finished before the army marched
